Package multiplayerserver.packets

Class PacketRegistry

java.lang.Object
multiplayerserver.packets.PacketRegistry
public class PacketRegistry extends Object
Tracks all the different packet classes, has packet specific handlers, and serializes and parses packets.

  • Method Details

    • registerPacket

      public <T extends Packet> void registerPacket(Class<T> clazz)
      Register a packet for packet parsing. Server doesn't need to register packets that are just forwarded to clients. Need to call register() if you want to react to receiving a packet type. Don't need to call this if you call register(). Required for when you want to react to a packet with a global or default handler, not needed otherwise. If a client can receive unregistered packets that you don't want to react to, you can disable warnings, or just register them using registerPacket(). Custom packet classes need to extend Packet.

      Usage: 

       registry.registerPacket(MovePacket.class)
 registry.registerPacket(ChatPacket.class)
      Type Parameters:
      T -
      Parameters:
      clazz -

    • register

      public <T extends Packet> void register(Class<T> clazz, Consumer<T> handler)
      Register a packet and set a handler for that packet type. Needs to be called for all the packets you want to handle in that client/server. Server doesn't need to register packets that are just forwarded to clients. Use separate PacketRegistry instance for server and clients.

      If you don't want to handle a packet, but want to be able to parse it, (for example for default/global handler) you need to call registerPacket() on the packet type.

      Packet classes need to extend Packet.

      Usage: registry.register(MovePacket.class, handlerFunction);

      Create handlerFunction (Consumer) with one of these ways (it accepts a Packet subclass):

      • Lambda expression:
        • One-liner: movePacket -> game.movePlayer(movePacket);

        • In block form:
          • 
     Consumer<MovePacket> handlerFunction = movePacket -> {
         game.movePlayer(movePacket);
     };
      • Reference a method that has the same input and return value.
        • You can reference it statically with ClassName::methodName
        • and non-statically with this::methodName or objectVariable::methodName
      Like this: 
        registry.register(MovePacket.class, move -> game.movePlayer(move));
  registry.register(ChatPacket.class, packetHandler::addChatMessage);
      handlerFunction can also be null (or just call registerPacket), in which case you can set up global handler function, or a default handler function. You can also use only the global function.
      Type Parameters:
      T -
      Parameters:
      clazz -
      handler -

    • parsePacket

      public Packet parsePacket(String payload) throws com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException
      Takes the payload String that has "className:" + "{jsonData}" and parses it into a Packet. Gets the packet type from the registered className. Prints a warning and returns null if packet type not registered.
      Parameters:

      Returns:
